label: Applied comparative sociological morphology to India’s regional kinship and caste systems
description: Trained in comparative anthropology and sociology, Karve systematically mapped how regional marriage rules and clan structures govern social solidarity across India.
dialecticalTension: Adapts European sociological method to non-Western polycentric kinship orders.

label: Provided empirical kinship foundations for analyzing caste endogamy and women’s vulnerability
description: Karve’s distinction between northern exogamous patrilocal kinship and southern cross-cousin marriage directly informed Chakravarti’s analysis of Brahmanical patriarchy.
dialecticalTension: Transforms descriptive kinship sociology into feminist structural critique of caste.

label: Empirically established the north-south kinship divide later linked to women’s land rights
description: Agarwal built directly upon Karve’s mapping of northern versus southern/northeastern kinship norms to explain regional disparities in women’s agricultural land claims.
dialecticalTension: Connects classical kinship anthropology to feminist political economy.
historicalContext: South Asian gender and property studies.
